Seminar Title:

Bismuth MOF derived ternary nano-heterostructure materials for environmental remediation and activation of atmospheric molecules

Abstract:

Design of high throughput semiconductor photocatalysts for solar radiation assisted aqueous pollutant and microbe remediation as well as activation of atmospheric molecules to valued chemicals is a promising field of research. In this thesis, a series of high surface area &alpha-Bi2O3 based ternary heterostructure photocatalysts were prepared through metal organic framework (MOF) derived route and studied for above applications. Initially, the Bi-trimesic acid (Bi-TMA) MOF with cuboidal nanorod morphology was synthesized by a facile solvothermal route. The simple air calcination of the Bi-TMA MOF led to the formation crystalline &alpha-Bi2O3 phase with rod shaped morphology. The MOF derived protocol was subsequently tailored for in situ one-pot synthesis of binary nanocomposite oxides. By careful choice of reaction parameters, metal salt precursors and using Bi-MOF as scaffold, four different nanocomposite oxides namely Sr6Bi2O9-&alpha-Bi2O3, BiVO4-&alpha-Bi2O3, Bi4Ti3O12-&alpha-Bi2O3 and Bi18CrO30-&alpha-Bi2O3 were prepared. All the binary composites retained the cuboidal rod shape morphology of &alpha-Bi2O3 phase. The Sr6Bi2O9, Bi4Ti3O12 and Bi18CrO30 semiconductors appeared as high aspect nanosheets in the composites whereas the BiVO4 phase expressed itself as spherical nanoparticles. The MOF derived nanocomposite oxides were subsequently used as high surface area platforms for decoration of plasmonic metal nanoparticles (Ag), low band gap metal ferrite (CuFe2O4) and metal sulfide (Cd0.5Zn0.5S, MoS2) nanostructures to prepare ternary photocatalysts. The as-synthesized ternary heterostructures were demonstrated as efficient photocatalyst for cirprofloxacin and mesotrione herbicide degradation, antibiotic-resistant bacteria and activation of O2 and N2 to H2O2 and NH3. The important results obtained and conclusions drawn from these studies will be presented in the defense seminar.
